title: Four Reasons to Add Beans to Your Diet
paragraphs: Beans, chickpeas, lentils and dry peas, which are collectively known as pulses, are among the most affordable foods available. Yet according to one study, only about one in three American adults eats them regularly. Here are four reasons why you might want to add more of them to your diet.
1. They may be good for your heart

A study published in the journal Current Developments in Nutrition in 2026 analyzed data on 46,939 adults in the United States. It found that each additional daily serving of pulses, which is about a quarter of a cup when cooked, was associated with a 19% lower prevalence of cardiometabolic diseases, a group of conditions that includes heart disease, stroke and diabetes. In addition, a 2026 review of 28 trials reportedly found that eating beans significantly lowered levels of LDL, or "bad," cholesterol.

Another 2026 study, which looked at 17,234 American adults, found that people who regularly ate pulses had higher-quality diets overall. They consumed more fiber, protein, iron, magnesium, potassium and folate, and they were less likely to have nutrient deficiencies. According to the study, eating just one and a half cups of pulses a week improved overall diet quality, while eating three cups a week led to even greater benefits.
3. They are a healthy source of protein
Unlike many sources of animal protein, beans provide protein together with fiber, vitamins and minerals, while being naturally low in saturated fat and containing no cholesterol.
4. They can help you feel full
Because beans contain both fiber and protein, they are digested slowly, which can help you feel full for longer. Their fiber also supports healthy digestion and a healthy gut.

However, it is worth noting that the studies mentioned above were observational, so they cannot prove that eating pulses directly causes these benefits. Some of the research was also promoted by industry groups. Nevertheless, beans remain a simple and inexpensive way to make meals healthier.
